subject: deployment mode economics & pilot terms
body_messages:
From: Simon Park <simon@brightleaf.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: deployment model & cost comparators

Thanks for the call earlier, Michael — quick recap from my side and a couple of asks so we can move to the pricing stage.

Summary of BrightLeaf needs:
- Product: customer-facing chat assistant (real-time) + nightly batch embeddings for search
- Typical traffic: ~3M generated tokens/day (avg), spikes up to ~6M/day during peak windows
- Latency SLO: 200ms p95 for chat; lower is better
- Data requirements: US-only residency for PII, SOC2 compliance required
- Security: need audit logs and KMS support for keys

Primary question: we want a side-by-side cost comparison of Hosted API (per-token), Dedicated (reserved capacity commits), and Private (VPC/on-prem) for pilot -> production. Please show: required commit size, expected monthly cost, and a short note on operational responsibilities for each mode.

Also: procurement contact is procurement@brightleaf.ai; they may need an initial statement of work and pilot terms. If possible, include an estimated SLA credit/penalty model for incidents that breach latency SLOs.

Thanks — can you share a short spreadsheet and a one-pager?

Simon
Head of Platform
BrightLeaf Analytics

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Park <simon@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-11T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment model & cost comparators

Simon — thanks for the clear summary. Attached are our discovery notes and a first-pass cost model (prelim-cost-model.xlsx). High level thoughts below; we can formalize numbers once we lock sample payloads and targets.

Quick comparison (ballpark, USD, monthly):
1) Hosted API (pay-as-you-go, per-token)
- Pricing assumption used: $0.0009 per generated token (illustrative; final depends on model choice and profile).
- For 3M tokens/day -> ~90M tokens/month -> ~ $81k/month.
- Pros: Zero ops, fastest time-to-value, Redwood handles runtime and keys.
- Cons: Higher unit cost at scale; less isolation of compute.

2) Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity)
- Example commit: 6x A10-equivalent GPUs reserved to comfortably support 6M peak/day with room for concurrency and batching.
- Monthly reserved cost (example): $28k–$40k/month depending on region and burst policy.
- When amortized against token throughput, this yields ~ $0.0003–$0.00045 per token (model, quantization, and batching dependent).
- Pros: Predictable throughput and lower per-token economics; Redwood manages serving runtime; data isolation within tenant.
- Cons: Requires commit; autoscaling/burst policies need calibration.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- One-time platform license + infra ops. Pilot model: customer-managed VPC deployment with our private control plane; or on-prem appliance for regulated use.
- Estimated first-month cost (license + infra resourcing): $80k–$150k (wide range depending on on-prem hardware and setup).
- Pros: Maximum isolation/compliance control; full data residency.
- Cons: Customer ops responsibility (unless purchasing managed private), longer lead time.

SLA and pilot suggestions:
- Pilot: 6 weeks, limited to US region, with a canary traffic split and rollback window.
- SLA: Standard offering is 99.9% uptime + latency goals; we can propose credits for p95 breaches (e.g., 5% credit for >3 incidents/month or sustained >200ms p95).

Next steps I propose:
- Internal pricing review (Lauren / Rishi): confirm reserve sizing and final numbers
- Send pilot SOW + budgetary estimate to procurement@brightleaf.ai (Vanessa to own)
- Schedule a 60-minute technical demo (we can include private deployment overview)

I attached BL-discovery-notes.pdf and the spreadsheet. Vanessa / Lauren / Rishi — any immediate adjustments to the numbers?

Best,
Michael
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment model & cost comparators

Rishi — quick internal note on pricing approach and asks from procurement.

Observations on Michael's model:
- Hosted per-token calc looks OK for a ballpark; we should show a second hosted SKU with committed discounts (e.g., 15% at >= $200k/mo spend) to give BrightLeaf runway to compare against Dedicated.
- Dedicated sizing: suggest we model a conservative and an aggressive commit: conservative = 4 GPU equivalent (~$20k/mo), aggressive = 8 GPU equivalent (~$45k/mo). Include cost-per-token curves at different utilization (40%, 70%, 90%).
- Private: break out license vs infra vs managed-service fee. For procurement, give a 12-month TCO estimate and a separate 1-month pilot pricing line item.

Procurement asks we should be ready for:
- Quick SOW with pilot acceptance criteria
- Data handling appendix (SOC2 statements, KMS integration steps)
- Sample SLA forward language (credits table + incident response times)

I'll draft the SOW template and the 2-sheet cost model they can hand to procurement. Michael: can you set up a 30-min alignment call with sales engineering and cloud ops for Friday? Vanessa: can you take point on sending the SOW once we have crisp numbers?

-Lauren
Director, Strategic Accounts

From: Simon Park <simon@brightleaf.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightleaf.ai
Date: 2026-11-13T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment model & cost comparators

Thanks — that all looks reasonable as a starting point. Two quick items from procurement and product: 

1) Procurement: please include a pilot SOW and estimated MSA redlines (procurement@brightleaf.ai). They want clarity on termination, data deletion, and indemnity for PII.
2) Product: is Redwood able to support a short on-prem pilot for a subset of traffic? If yes, we'd like a technical checklist and an estimated lead time for on-prem appliance (if applicable).

Also: SLA credits proposal will be evaluated by their legal; please include examples and the metrics tied to p95 latency and availability.

Let us know available times next week for a 60-min demo and a procurement intro.

-simon
